item.title: Deep-level engineering in aluminum nitride (AlN) enables reliable photodetection in extreme conditions
item.description: arXiv:2606.07807v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Semiconductor photodetectors are conventionally optimized for sensing weak optical signals, and they typically saturate at low-to-moderate light intensity. Here, we demonstrate AlN photodetectors that exhibit non-saturating linear response to ultra-bright, sub-bandgap light exceeding 40 $\mathrm{W/cm^2}$ (over 400 Suns). The photodetector further shows undistorted linear response at elevated temperature, up to at least 300 $\mathrm{^\circ C}$.

item.description: Xufeng Zhang is using magnets to make computers more power efficient at the quantum level. item.title: Path-Integrated Polarization Rotation Signatures in Subsea Networks: Cable Geometry Effects in 2023 Turkey Earthquakes
item.description: arXiv:2609.20527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze polarization data streamed from a commercial coherent transponder, used in MedNautilus link, during 2023 Turkey earthquakes. We show how earthquake features and cable geometry fundamentally govern the optical polarization response, taking the first steps for detailed interpretation in designing fiber-based seismic sensing systems.

item.title: A Simplified Model for Linear Mode Coupling in Multimode Fibers with Experimental Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2609.20617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel surrogate model for linear coupling in graded-index multimode fibers that is computationally more efficient than existing models, and can be tuned through a single measurable parameter. The model is benchmarked numerically and experimentally on a 90-polarization-mode fiber.

item.description: The vast majority of modern quantum technologies—from quantum cryptography to the quantum internet to the quantum computer—rely on one essential element: the transmission of photons. Two qubits (two atoms, for example) exchange information: One qubit emits a photon, and the other qubit absorbs it.
